variables.problem: I'm pretraining a ViT image encoder with self-supervision and need features semantic enough for linear probing. Augmentation-invariance methods depend on hand-crafted view augmentations (crops, colour jitter) that bake in biases and don't carry over to other modalities, and reconstructing raw pixels gives low-level features that need heavy fine-tuning. I need a pretraining task that yields semantic image representations without hand-crafted augmentations.
variables.tried: Contrastive learning with heavy multi-crop augmentations.

rubric: A good idea borrows BERT's masked-prediction pretraining (hide part of the input, predict the hidden part from context) and cites the BERT section that defines it; the rationale says what is masked in an image and what is predicted.

variables.problem: Our food-scooping robot runs a diffusion policy whose sampling is steered by a learned spillage predictor: throughout denoising we estimate the clean trajectory, score its spillage risk and push the gradient back into the sample. The robot controller runs at 10 Hz, and generating each guided action chunk eats most of that cycle, so the policy lags behind and cannot replan quickly as the food shifts. We need guided trajectory generation that keeps up with the control loop without losing trajectory quality or the spillage guidance.
variables.tried: Checking spillage once after sampling instead of guiding during denoising (reduces spillage less).

rubric: A good idea borrows shortcut models (one network conditioned on the step size, sampling in one or a few steps) and cites the section that defines them; the rationale says how guidance fits a few-step sampler.

variables.problem: We want a language model that isn't tied to left-to-right decoding, so it can infill, follow controls and generate tokens in parallel. Our non-autoregressive generators over discrete tokens trail autoregressive LMs by a wide margin in log-likelihood at the same parameter count. We need a generation framework for discrete text that closes that gap.

rubric: A good idea borrows the image-diffusion recipe (gradually corrupt data, learn to reverse the corruption) and cites the section describing diffusion training/sampling; the rationale says what the corruption becomes for discrete tokens.

variables.problem: Our vision-language-action policy feeds dense visual tokens from several camera views into an LLM at every control step, and attention over those tokens dominates inference cost. Fixed-ratio token pruning helps, but redundancy changes over an episode: coarse reaching motions need few visual tokens, fine-grained grasping needs many. We need a way to decide, per step, which visual tokens get processed and how many, under a compute budget.
variables.tried: Fixed-ratio pruning of visual tokens by text relevance.

rubric: A good idea borrows Expert Choice routing (the processing units choose their top-k tokens under a fixed capacity, so the number of tokens per unit is set by a budget) and cites the section that defines it; the rationale maps experts/capacity onto token retention.

variables.problem: We train manipulation policies with RL on one robot arm and want to reuse them on arms with different kinematics, state and action spaces, or move them from simulation to a real robot, without re-tuning rewards in the new domain. A policy learned in one robot's state/action space does not transfer, and we have no carefully paired data between the two robots. We need a policy trained on one robot to work on another with little data from the new one.
variables.tried: Retraining from scratch on the new arm; hand-written joint mappings.

rubric: A good idea borrows ALIGN's contrastive alignment of two modalities into one embedding space from large noisy pairs and cites the section that defines it; the rationale says what the two 'modalities' and the noisy pairs are for two robots.

variables.problem: Our hierarchical VLA policy (a vision-language backbone plus a generative action head) conditions only on the current observation, so it loses track of task progress, repeats or skips sub-steps on long tasks and produces jittery trajectories. Feeding the full observation and action history into the transformer is too expensive at our control rate. We need the policy to carry long-horizon context cheaply at every step.
variables.tried: Stacking the last few frames as extra context.

rubric: A good idea borrows Mamba's selective state space (a fixed-size recurrent state with input-dependent updates, linear in sequence length) and cites the section that defines it; the rationale says what the state summarises for the policy.

variables.problem: Our autoregressive VLA policy has to turn continuous action chunks into discrete tokens. Per-dimension binning gives long token sequences that make decoding slow, while compressing harder loses reconstruction fidelity and hurts precise manipulation. We need an action representation that is both compact and faithful, and that generalises across tasks and robots.
variables.tried: Uniform per-dimension binning; DCT-based compression of action chunks.

rubric: A good idea borrows byte-pair-encoding subword units (start from symbols and repeatedly merge the most frequent adjacent pair into a new vocabulary entry) and cites the BPE section that defines it; the rationale says what the symbols and merges are for action chunks.

variables.problem: Real humanoid-robot data is orders of magnitude too scarce to pretrain a generalist policy, so we train on a heterogeneous mixture: a little real-robot data, human videos, and a large share of synthetically generated trajectories from simulation and video-generation models. We plan to scale mainly by generating more of that synthetic data. We need the policy's real-world behaviour to keep improving as the generated share grows.
variables.tried: Up-weighting the small real-robot set during training.

rubric: A good idea borrows the model-collapse finding (training recursively on generated data loses the tails of the real distribution; keeping real data in the mix prevents it) and cites the section that explains it; the rationale says what to monitor or keep fixed in the robot data loop.

variables.problem: Our image-retrieval system takes the top 100 candidates from a global-descriptor nearest-neighbour search and reranks them with a verifier that matches the query against each candidate. The query object can appear anywhere in a candidate image, at any scale and aspect ratio, so verifying many location hypotheses per candidate is too slow, and checking only the whole image misses small or off-centre matches. We need the reranking stage to handle matches at arbitrary position and scale without exhaustively testing every location.
variables.tried: Whole-image rescoring with the global descriptor; sliding-window matching at a few scales (too slow).

rubric: The user's own example. A good idea borrows Faster R-CNN's anchor boxes (a fixed set of reference boxes at several scales and aspect ratios per feature-map position, each scored and refined by regression) and cites the section that defines them; the rationale says how anchors become match hypotheses for reranking.

variables.problem: Our vision-language-action policy follows language instructions well on its training tasks but fails on new tasks and unfamiliar objects. Collecting demonstrations and fine-tuning for every new task is too slow for deployment, while operators can easily show the robot a couple of images of what they want (a goal photo, frames from a demonstration). We need the policy to pick up a new task at deployment from a handful of example images, without retraining.
variables.tried: Per-task fine-tuning on about 50 demonstrations; rephrasing the language instruction.

rubric: The user's own example. A good idea borrows GPT-3's in-context learning (task demonstrations placed in the prompt, no gradient updates) and cites the section that defines it; the rationale says how example images become the policy's prompt.
